A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same USP research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching renamed baselines and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original profile-quality assessments, simulator experiments, human evaluations, ablations and downstream LLM evaluations in Tables 2–7 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds an attribute-only ablation, another case study and numerical annotator-agreement reporting.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains profile extraction and polishing, conditional SFT, density-based profile sampling, and PPO with cycle-consistency and AI-detection rewards. Revised equations and additional implementation details do not establish a changed implemented method; USAP is an ablation control.

E1.justification: Both versions use English LMSYS-USP conversations, Persona-Chat and ConvAI2 for profile-quality assessment, and majority, minority and virtual profiles for downstream evaluation. The added ablation and illustrative case do not establish expanded dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds the attribute-only USAP (w/o RLCC) comparator in Table 6. The original comparator sets remain; the GPT-4o and LLaMA3 labels replace DialogueGPT and ProfileGPT names without introducing different baselines.

E3.justification: The added Table 6 experiment compares raw attributes against polished profiles while disabling RLCC in both configurations. Existing dataset splits, metrics and the downstream 100-majority/100-minority/100-virtual profile design remain unchanged. Newly specified settings for retained experiments are disclosures rather than evidence of reruns.

E4.justification: Section 6.1 adds a controlled test of profile polishing, and Section 6.3/Table 8 adds a case examining explicit trait copying versus concrete, implicit expression. The existing reward-weight ablation, sampling analysis, downstream turn analysis and appendix case studies remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports profile-rating means with qualitative agreement claims; v3 Table 10 additionally reports one-point agreement rates of 89.2%, 74.3% and 88.4%. v3 also identifies the retained kappa statistics as within-group measures and explains annotator pairing. These are reporting additions, not evidence of additional experimental runs.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 2–5 and 7 remain unchanged after matching baseline names. Table 6 adds USAP results, including ESR 17 and r-DPC 57.47; v3 also adds agreement percentages and Table 8's qualitative outputs. Some displayed word-puzzle case excerpts are edited without establishing a new experiment.

T1.justification: Section 3 changes the formal task objective from dialogue-distance minimization in v1 Equations 1–2 to an explicit weighted combination of utterance and dialogue distances in v3 Equation 1, introducing alpha and defining ground-truth context. This is a limited mathematical reformulation; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain implicit-profile extraction, profile-conditioned simulation with SFT and RLCC, and distribution-aware sampling. Both versions claim superior authenticity and diversity, comparable consistency, and useful dynamic multi-turn LLM evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 expands the precision-versus-recall rationale for RLCC and interprets the new polishing control and case study. It acknowledges a remaining gap from real human behavior while retaining the dataset and language limitations. However, v1's specific discussion of harmful dataset content and unsafe profile-driven behavior is removed.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies learning rates, maximum length, KL coefficient, RL epoch count, evaluation sample counts and annotator qualifications/assignment, and reports open-source release instead of a planned release. Conversely, v1's full baseline prompt/model-version table and decoding settings disappear. Reproducibility documentation therefore changes substantially; hardware and training durations largely relocate from Appendix B.1 to Section 5.2.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused references and positioning concerning profile-dialogue alignment, role-playing and static multi-turn benchmarks, including Chen et al. (2023), Yu et al. (2024), Lu et al. (2024), Kong et al. (2025) and Bai et al. (2024). Madotto et al. (2019) and Tseng et al. (2024) are removed, while the broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, task formulation, method explanations, results discussion and appendices undergo extensive rewriting. Profile sampling moves before RLCC, a Configurations subsection incorporates earlier appendix material, baseline terminology is standardized, and acknowledgments and affiliation text change.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, Figure 3 is reformatted and reannotated, Table 6 expands, and a new case-study Table 8 appears. The baseline setup table and three human-evaluation interface figures are removed. Token-length statistics move from a table into prose, while retained guidelines, plots and prompt displays are regrouped.

improvement.justification: The new polishing ablation directly tests a previously untested design choice, while added training hyperparameters and annotator-agreement statistics make the existing evidence easier to assess. These provide a modest quality gain alongside clearer exposition. The gain is tempered by unchanged evaluation coverage and the removal of baseline prompts, decoding details and the specific safety discussion.
